audit.why: Camille holding levels 1-5 and reclaiming the lane at two items matches 45.45% over 11 games - a losing matchup where Kassadin's usual scaling payoff does not arrive, because Hextech Ultimatum manufactures the isolated duel he cannot win. The chart already reflects that; only the wording needed sharpening.

audit.whatIsWrong: No spike carried a number, and the two-item danger window never named the ult's cooldown.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s, Tactical Sweep 15/14/13/12/11s, and The Hextech Ultimatum 140/115/90s. Her ult being on 140s at rank 1 is why you can walk the side lane between casts.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[9].t, dosFull[0].d and loading now carry them.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot was called a 'stun' in eight places. Riot's text says it knocks up. Two big interactions were also missing: (1) Tactical Sweep only slows, deals extra damage and heals her from its OUTER half, so stepping toward her denies all three; (2) Adaptive Defenses gives her a shield matched to your damage type whenever she autos you, so her auto on you pre-loads a magic shield against your Null Sphere.
audit.why: Riot: 'Camille pulls herself to a wall, leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing'; 'Enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille'; 'Basic attacks on champions grant a shield equal to a percentage of Camille's maximum health against their damage type'.
audit.corrected: Replaced stun with knock-up throughout, and wrote both interactions into report[5].t, dosFull[0], content.spikes[0].text and content.early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization made no mention of Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Tactical Sweep heals her every time its outer half clips you, on an 11-15 second cycle - that is the sustain that wins her the extended trades this lane is full of.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now buys anti-heal against Tactical Sweep.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer called Camille 'he'/'his' and described her as a juggernaut.
audit.why: Camille is female and is a diver-duelist; the juggernaut line is boilerplate from another matchup.
audit.corrected: Fixed tldr, winCon, report[0].t, report[1].t, tradeGood, tradeBad, dosFull[1].d, dosFull[2].t, dontsFull[0].t, dontsFull[2].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are the worst stretch of my game and Camille knows it — I have only Null Sphere, no escape, and my Q is mana-hungry and short-ranged while she has a wall-dash stun (Hookshot) and a W cone (Tactical Sweep) that heals her off its outer edge. I cannot trade: if I step up to throw a Q, she Hookshots me into the wall and cashes a free all-in capped by her Q true-damage proc. Last-hit from maximum range, eat the poke, and don't burn the mana I need for Nether Blade.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are the worst stretch of my game and Camille knows it - I have only Null Sphere, no escape, and my Q is mana-hungry and short while she has a wall knock-up (Hookshot) and a W cone (Tactical Sweep) that heals her off its outer half. If I step up to throw a Q, she hooks a wall, knocks me up and cashes a free all-in. When the cone fires I step toward her, not away, because the inner half neither slows nor heals. Last-hit from maximum range and keep the mana I need for Nether Blade.

notes: Hookshot was called a stun in eight places across both layers; Riot's text says it knocks up, which matters because tenacity behaves differently and because a knock-up cannot be shortened. The Hextech Ultimatum 'anchors' you to its area per Riot's text - I wrote the anchor but deliberately did NOT claim whether Riftwalk can leave the ring, because the kit data does not say and that is exactly the kind of claim a player would bet a game on. Logged in unverified. Precision Protocol's true-damage claim was already on the page and the kit carries a trueDamage flag for it, so I left it standing but did not amplify it.
